subject: Changes to language for new versions of Stan

messages.author: 1fe638ac9008754d
messages.subject: Changes to language for new versions of Stan
parts:
Hello all,

Forgive this question - it is similar to a question I asked about 5 months ago, about upcoming changes to the Stan language. However, given the time that's passed I wanted to ask again, about upcoming updates to the Stan language.

Basically I wanted to know, is there consensus on which parts of the language will be deprecated in the new version of Stan? In particular, in the past there has been discussed of removing the "~" statement, and I wanted to ask whether this is likely to occur? Otherwise, are there any other parts of the language that are likely to become deprecated? If so, then do you know when these might happen?

The reason I ask is because I am writing a guide for my students.

Best,

Ben

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Changes to language for new versions of Stan
parts:
I don't think we'll be deprecating ~ any time soon. And
nothing else is scheduled to be deprecated.

The next big change for 2.12 will be allowing compound
declare/define, e.g.

real a = 5.7;

and vectorizing most of the unary functions. No other
big deprecations on the way.

We'll also be allowing ways for users to control whether
the ~ statements and _lpdf, _lpmf functions include
constant terms, but the default behavior won't change (not
included with ~, included with functions).

We're probably going to allow incrementing the Jacobian
in the transformed parameter block with the behavior that
the density increments won't be included for maximum likelihood.

Other than allowing some new data types (sparse matrices
and ragged arrays, no projected time of arrival), I don't anticipate
many changes. I tried to get all the deprecating changes in
one go.

- Bob

parts:
Bob, 

That's cool about the compound declare/define change. 

How difficult would it be to allow declarations in a block after some work being 
done? 

For example, let's say I want to declare an integer array in the transformed 
data block, but its size depends on something being computed in the
transformed data block. I can't currently do

transformed data {
// size = some work with data

int my_integer[size];
}

But I'd like to. A case is in declaring the u and v integer vectors 
for a sparse covariance matrix. 

Is such a change straightforward? 

Jim

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Changes to language for new versions of Stan
parts:
Not straightforward, but it's on our to-do list. Whether
we'll be able to do it for block variables as well as
local variables remains to be seen. Mitzi's got the
compound declare-define working for vectors and scalars
and just needs to fish the rest of the cases and tests through,
so this'll definiely get into 2.12.

I share your motivation about block variables and would
add that it's clearer when variables are declared and
defined as close as possible to where they're used (i.e,
as late as possible), even if there aren't any dependencies.

What I worry about is that it won't be clear what the set
of transformed parameters are if they're peppered into chunks
of code.

- Bob
